title: Update notebook cell
description: Update a cell by node_id. For a SQL or Python cell pass `code` to replace its source and re-run it, or omit code to re-run it unchanged (how you refresh a stale cell). For a markdown cell (cell_type 'markdown' in notebooks-get: prose, a heading, a table, a fenced block) pass `markdown` instead: it replaces that block only, runs nothing, and leaves every other cell untouched. That is how you fix wording in a notebook you already shared, instead of appending a correction or recreating it under a new URL. Read the ids with notebooks-get and edit against that same read, because a markdown cell's id is derived from its text and changes once the text changes. Waits up to ~45s and returns the result like notebooks-add-cell, plus stale_dependents: the downstream cells whose inputs this run invalidated. Nothing re-runs automatically — inspect each dependent and re-run it with this tool (no code) or fix it first, walking the graph one hop at a time. To refresh the whole notebook in one call instead, use notebooks-run. The run binds the notebook's current variables, so re-running (no code) is also how a cell picks up a changed variable value. Re-running a Python cell provisions the notebook's sandbox when none is running, and the user pays for it while it runs, so tell them its hourly_price the first time a run starts one.
